kind=design-and-schema; reason=Rejected: this design is built on wrong assumptions about the real codebase, called out as assumptions in the design itself. Real facts for the re-plan: (1) Persistence is Spring Data JDBC, not JPA/Hibernate - no @Entity, no JPQL. Link is an immutable record in package link, table name is plural `links` (not `link`), mapped with @Table/@Column from org.springframework.data.relational.core.mapping. Repositories extend CrudRepository and use @Modifying @Query with plain SQL. (2) There is no Flyway/Liquibase. Schema lives in url-shortener/src/main/resources/schema.sql, applied every startup via spring.sql.init.mode=always using CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS - the click_event DDL must be appended there, not a new Flyway migration file. (3) The real API prefix is /api/v1/links (not /api/links) - the existing stats endpoint is GET /api/v1/links/{code}/stats, so the new endpoint should be GET /api/v1/links/{code}/analytics. (4) Real class names: RedirectController (GET /{code:[0-9A-Za-z]{1,16}}), LinkService (method resolve(String code) already does the lookup, expiry check via Link.isExpired, and click-count increment, and already throws LinkNotFoundException/LinkExpiredException), ApiExceptionHandler (RestControllerAdvice extending ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, not GlobalExceptionHandler), AppProperties (ConfigurationProperties app, nested static getter/setter classes like RateLimit and Link - follow that same convention for any new analytics config instead of a new properties class). (5) A Clock bean already exists at config.ClockConfig (Clock.systemUTC()); reuse it, do not add another. (6) Link expiry already ships (see the existing LinkExpiredException / 410 Gone flow) - keep AC4 (no click event for expired links) consistent with that existing resolve() flow rather than inventing a new resolveAndRecord replacement from scratch; prefer extending the existing method/call chain. Please produce a revised design against these real facts.
